toc.title: Deploying, operating and where AWS runs

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. CLI: command line interface; SDK: software development kit; YAML: YAML Ain't Markup Language; CDK: Cloud Development Kit; IAM: Identity and Access Management

  • Choose among the console, the CLI, SDKs and infrastructure as code, for one-time and repeatable work
  • Explain what AWS CloudFormation, AWS Service Catalog and Service Quotas do
  • Tell cloud, hybrid and on-premises deployment models apart
  • Describe Regions, Availability Zones and edge locations, and how they relate
  • Decide when to use multiple Availability Zones and when multiple Regions

2Deploying, operating and where AWS runs

Running case

Tidewater Goes Global

  • Tidewater's customers in Europe see slow pages, and the team wants a second copy of the shop near them
  • Engineers build servers by clicking through the console, and no two environments match
  • Test and production must be identical and quick to rebuild
  • The warehouse system stays in the back office but must still talk to the cloud
  • Your job: choose how to deploy, operate and place the shop

Ways to Reach AWS

  • The AWS Management Console is a web-based interface for people: good for exploring and one-time tasks
  • The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) runs commands in a shell, so steps can be scripted and automated
  • AWS SDKs are libraries for languages such as Python, Java and JavaScript, so applications can call AWS services
  • The CLI and SDKs call the AWS service APIs directly; sending API requests yourself means signing them too
  • AWS CloudShell gives you the CLI in a browser tab, already signed in Beyond the guide

Exam tip

Everything in the console is also available through the API, the CLI and the SDKs.

Console, CLI, SDK or Template?

Tidewater needs to Best fit Why
Try a new service once Management Console Visual, no code, good for one-time work
Run the same steps every night AWS CLI script Commands can be saved, shared and scheduled
Let the shop's code create or read resources AWS SDK Calls AWS from your own application
Build the same whole environment every time Infrastructure as code A template makes it repeatable
  • One-time operation: the console is fine
  • Repeatable process: script it, or put it in a template
Exam tip

One-time and visual: console. Repeat and automate: CLI, SDK or a template.

Infrastructure as Code: AWS CloudFormation

  • Infrastructure as code means describing your infrastructure in text files that a tool turns into real resources
  • A CloudFormation template is a YAML or JSON file that lists resources and their settings
  • A stack is everything created from one template; you create, update and delete it as one unit
  • A change set previews an update, and a failed creation rolls back
  • Reuse one template for test and production, or in several Regions, and keep it in version control
  • The AWS CDK lets you write the same thing in a programming language Beyond the guide

Exam tip

Repeatable, consistent environments from a template: AWS CloudFormation.

Service Catalog and Service Quotas

Service What it does Remember
AWS Service Catalog An organization creates catalogs of approved IT services: products gathered in portfolios; users launch only approved products, within the constraints you set Approved, standard setups through self-service
Service Quotas View and manage your quotas (also called limits) in one place, and request increases A launch fails because an account or Region limit was reached
  • Each service sets default quotas per account or Region; some are adjustable
  • AWS Support might approve, deny or partly approve a request
Exam tip

Approved products for users: Service Catalog. Limits and increase requests: Service Quotas.

Deployment Models: Cloud, Hybrid and On-Premises

Model What it means Fits when
Cloud All parts of the application run in the cloud, built there or migrated You want the full benefit of the cloud
Hybrid Connects cloud resources to existing resources not in the cloud, most often on-premises Some systems must stay on site, or you move step by step
On-premises (private cloud) Resources in your own data center, using virtualization and management tools You need dedicated resources, with few cloud benefits
  • Services for hybrid arrive later: Direct Connect and VPN (virtual private network, Module 10), Storage Gateway (Module 8), AWS Outposts (Module 7)
Exam tip

Some systems in the cloud and some in your own data center, connected: hybrid.

Regions, Availability Zones and Edge Locations [Dates]

  • A Region is a physical location where AWS clusters data centers
  • Each Region has at least three isolated Availability Zones (AZs)
  • An AZ is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity
  • Edge locations sit in many more places, to deliver content close to users
  • As of 4 November 2026: AWS reports 39 Regions, 124 AZs and 750+ CloudFront points of presence; counts change, and other AWS pages differ

Exam tip

A Region contains Availability Zones; edge locations are separate and serve cached content.

Choosing a Region

  • Compliance and data residency: you choose the Region where your content is stored, and AWS will not move it out of that Region except as needed to provide the services or to comply with the law
  • Latency: pick a Region close to most of your users
  • Services and features: not every service is in every Region, so check availability
  • Cost: compare prices between Regions (Module 13)
  • Regions are independent: each one is isolated from the others
  • Newer Regions must be enabled in your account before you can use them Beyond the guide
Exam tip

Data must stay in a country: choose a Region there. Users far away: choose a Region near them.

3Availability, edge locations and practice

Availability Zones and High Availability

  • High availability means the application keeps working when a part of it fails
  • Each AZ has its own power, cooling and physical security, so AZs do not share a single point of failure
  • AZs are many kilometers apart, yet within 100 km (60 miles), joined by low-latency, high-bandwidth links with encrypted traffic
  • Run the application in at least two AZs behind a load balancer
  • If one AZ fails, the others keep serving customers

Exam tip

Survive a data center failure inside a Region: use multiple Availability Zones.

Multiple Regions: When and Why

Reason What it gives Tidewater example
Disaster recovery and business continuity The shop keeps serving if a whole Region is unavailable A copy of the shop in a second Region
Low latency Users are served from a Region near them European customers served from a Europe Region
Data sovereignty Data stays in a chosen country to meet the law Customer records kept in a Region inside that country
  • Multiple Regions make copying your setup important: one CloudFormation template can build the same stack in each Region
Exam tip

Whole-Region failure, distance from users or legal location: multiple Regions. One data center failing: multiple AZs.

Edge Locations: Content Close to Users

  • Edge locations (CloudFront points of presence) keep cached copies of your content near viewers
  • DNS sends each request to the edge location that serves it best, usually the nearest in latency
  • Cache hit: the edge returns the object. Cache miss: it fetches it from the origin, such as an Amazon S3 bucket, then caches it
  • Regional edge caches sit between the origin and the edge locations and keep content longer
  • Amazon CloudFront uses them (Module 10); AWS Local Zones place some services closer to big cities Beyond the guide

Exam tip

Faster delivery of content to distant users: edge locations, through CloudFront.

What the Exam Asks: Deploying and Global Infrastructure

  • Console, CLI, SDK or template: explore once, script it, call it from code, or rebuild the same environment
  • One-time or repeatable: console for one-time; CLI, SDK or template for repeatable
  • CloudFormation, Service Catalog or Service Quotas: build from a template, offer approved products, or manage limits
  • Cloud, hybrid or on-premises: all in AWS, connected to your data center, or only in your data center
  • Region, AZ or edge location: where data lives, a data center group inside a Region, or where cached content is served
  • Multi-AZ or multi-Region: survive a data center failure, or survive a Region failure and reach distant users
Exam tip

Match the failure or the need to the smallest unit that solves it.

Design Check: Tidewater Goes Global

Tidewater's need Choose
Test and production that match exactly CloudFormation template, one stack per environment
A nightly job that starts and stops test servers AWS CLI or SDK script on a schedule
Engineers exploring a new service for the first time Management Console
Only approved server setups for the support team AWS Service Catalog
A launch fails because the account hit a limit Service Quotas, then request an increase
The warehouse system stays on site but talks to the cloud Hybrid deployment
The shop survives the loss of one data center Servers in two or more AZs behind a load balancer
Product photos load slowly in Europe CloudFront edge locations, and a Europe Region
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Tidewater needs the same load balancer, servers and database created identically in a test account and a production account, and rebuilt quickly when needed. Which approach fits best?

  • ABuild each environment by hand in the console and write down the steps
  • BDescribe the resources in a CloudFormation template and build a stack from it
  • CAsk each engineer to type the commands from memory in AWS CloudShell
  • DUse Service Quotas to copy the settings from the test account to the production account
Show the answer

Answer: B. A CloudFormation template describes the resources once, and each stack built from it is consistent and repeatable. Manual steps and commands typed from memory drift between environments, and Service Quotas manages limits rather than copying settings.

S2A developer wants to automate a nightly task that starts and stops test servers on a schedule. Which approach fits best?

  • ASign in to the Management Console every night and click through each of the steps
  • BAsk an administrator to run the steps by hand when time allows
  • CWrite a script that uses the AWS CLI or an AWS SDK and run it on a schedule
  • DUse AWS Service Catalog to launch a new copy of the servers each night
Show the answer

Answer: C. The CLI and the SDKs call the AWS APIs from code, so steps can be saved, repeated and scheduled. The console suits one-time visual work, manual requests do not repeat reliably, and Service Catalog offers approved products, not scheduled tasks.

S3Tidewater keeps its warehouse system in its own data center and connects it to its resources in AWS. Which deployment model is this?

  • AHybrid, which connects cloud resources to existing on-premises ones
  • BCloud, in which every part of the application runs in AWS
  • COn-premises, in which all of the resources stay in its own data center
  • DMulti-Region, in which copies run in different parts of the world
Show the answer

Answer: A. A hybrid deployment connects cloud-based resources with existing resources that are not in the cloud, most often on-premises. A cloud deployment runs every part in AWS, an on-premises deployment uses no cloud, and multi-Region describes where copies run rather than a deployment model.

S4What is an AWS Availability Zone?

  • AA location that caches copies of content close to viewers in cities around the world
  • BA separate AWS account that a team uses to keep its own workloads apart from others
  • CA geographic area that always contains exactly two data centers and nothing else
  • DOne or more discrete data centers with redundant power and networking in a Region
Show the answer

Answer: D. An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity in an AWS Region. Caching content near viewers describes an edge location, and an AWS account is a different concept altogether.

S5Tidewater runs its web servers in one Availability Zone, and an outage there would take the shop offline. What is the simplest way to improve availability?

  • AMove the web servers to a larger instance type, still in the same zone as before
  • BRun the web servers in two Availability Zones behind a load balancer
  • CCopy the web servers into a different AWS account in the same zone
  • DAdd an edge location in front of the web servers, which all stay in the same zone
Show the answer

Answer: B. Availability Zones do not share a single point of failure, so servers in two zones behind a load balancer keep serving if one fails. A bigger instance, another account or an edge location still leave every server in the failed zone.

S6Tidewater's European customers see slow loads of product photos that are stored in a Region in the United States. Which approach delivers the photos faster?

  • AUse Amazon CloudFront to cache the photos at edge locations near them
  • BAdd a second Availability Zone for the photo storage in the same US Region of AWS
  • CTurn on AWS CloudTrail logging in the Region that holds the product photos
  • DIncrease the size and the number of the web servers in the US Region
Show the answer

Answer: A. CloudFront caches content at edge locations close to viewers, so the photos travel a shorter distance. Another Availability Zone in the same Region adds resilience rather than proximity, CloudTrail records activity, and larger servers do not shorten the distance.

S7Which TWO are valid reasons to run a workload in more than one AWS Region? (Select TWO.)

  • ATo avoid the need for backups and encryption
  • BTo keep serving customers if an entire Region becomes unavailable
  • CTo make Availability Zones unnecessary inside each Region
  • DTo meet a rule that data must be stored in a specific country
  • ETo share one set of IAM users across every account automatically
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Multiple Regions support disaster recovery and business continuity, and they let you place data in a country to satisfy data sovereignty rules; low latency for distant users is a third reason. Backups, encryption and Availability Zones are still needed, and IAM users are not shared between accounts automatically.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Access the console is for people and one-time work; the CLI and SDKs call the same APIs for scripts and applications
Infrastructure as code CloudFormation builds consistent stacks from YAML or JSON templates
Governance Service Catalog offers approved products; Service Quotas manages limits
Deployment models cloud, hybrid (cloud plus your own data center) and on-premises
Global infrastructure Regions hold at least three AZs; edge locations serve cached content
Resilience multiple AZs for a data center failure; multiple Regions for a Region failure, low latency or data sovereignty
